words.gloss: as large as a palmyra palm

literal: Even if one does a help of the size of a millet seed, those who understand the value will consider it as of the size of a palmyra palm.
translation: Even if the help rendered is as small as a millet seed, those who truly understand its value will cherish it as huge as a palmyra palm.
modern: தினையளவு மிகச்சிறிய உதவியை ஒருவர் செய்தாலும், அதன் பயனை அறிந்தவர்கள் அதனைப் பனையளவு பெரிய உதவியாகக் கருதுவார்கள்.
explanation: This couplet highlights how the recipients of a favor evaluate its worth. The poet contrasts two well-known objects of vastly different sizes: the tiny millet seed (thinai) and the massive palmyra palm (panai). Those who truly understand the value of gratitude and the timely nature of help (payan terivar) do not look at the physical scale of the assistance. Instead, they magnify even the smallest act of kindness, treating it as a monumental favor.
